correctness.rationale: Each selected core forces inclusion of its mate in a fort; an unselected core's mate is required with one selected core neighbor, forbidden with zero, and removable with at least two. No nonempty fort has empty core support. In a tree, three fort neighbors at an outside vertex allow an entire branch to be dropped. Once there are at most two, retaining one component of the two-step link graph requires no new mates and gives a smaller fort if the graph is disconnected. Conversely, any subfort's support must take both ends or neither across each link since the middle core's mate is absent, so connectedness proves minimality. On a path the supports are contiguous length-k parity runs; their weights are 2k plus the number of ends that do not touch a core endpoint. For even n the two maximal parity runs each touch one endpoint; for odd n one maximal run touches both endpoints and the other touches neither. They give the only size-n+1 forts. Singletons at endpoints give the only size-three forts; endpoint intervals and interior intervals realize the intervening odd and even weights. The total is the sum of interval counts over the two parity classes. Each nonempty A gives a distinct fort. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In W(T), the core support A and its selected mates force the canonical S(A); the maximum-degree condition makes A independent. On every core path joining members of A, an edge joining two outside cores would violate the cut condition. The path therefore alternates; each intervening outside core already has two neighbors in A and no selected mate, so suppressing it gives exactly a link. Conversely connected links put all core support in one component after deleting all outside–outside edges. Every pendant in S(A) attaches to this component, directly or through its core with one neighbor in A. A is independent by bipartiteness, and three selected neighbors of an outside core would occupy distinct components of T-v with no links across them. Thus the original test is exactly the earlier criterion in these coordinates.

originality.rationale: Cameron–Li Theorem 3.3 on arbitrary trees directly yields the main characterization. The link graph is the suppressed alternating subtree allowed by their cut condition, and the comb polynomial and size claims are mechanical counts of intervals in its two parity classes. This is demonstrated prior coverage, not a failure to find the same polynomial in print.
residual_risks: The precise version in which Theorem 3.3 first appeared was not established; the inspected March 2026 version predates the frozen finding.
